title: The auction ladder facts, the ladder states, the trigger, the three consumed owner contracts and the requirement id have no single source in the app slice of RWB-E5-019
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E5-019, its Acceptance criteria, Data, Endpoints, Screen and states and Permission checks tables); Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (A2.19.1, A2.19.2, A2.19.3.1, A2.19.3.3, A2.19.4); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 (T3.1, T3.2, T4, T5.1, T5.2, T5.3, T6.1, appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-LIT-63 to R-LIT-67); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (feature row FEAT-LIT-19); _work/msr/context/S4.md (ownership rows of S4: two tables, five REST operations, zero events, zero jobs, one workflow)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 1, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10; s8 BR4, BR5, BR6, BR7; s9 State transitions; s11 Data; s12.2; s12.3; s12.4; s12.5; s12.6; s12.7; s13 Solution plan; s14; s19 Out of scope; CON s2, s3, s7 AC1, AC3, AC4, AC5 and AC6, s11, s12.2, s12.5, s12.6, s12.7, s13, s19
description: RWB-E5-019 follows the enforcement auction through the 100, 90, 80 and 70 percent steps of official value, and R-LIT-63 to R-LIT-67 name the round, the price basis of official value, the official value, the round result, the bid amount and the auction date as the facts each step tests. The data model gives this service two tables, legal_action (DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014) and hearing (DF-LEG-024 to DF-LEG-029), and neither carries an auction round, a price basis, an official value, a round result, a bid or an auction date, while LOV-LEGAL-STATUS is OPEN, FILED, JUDGMENT, ENFORCING, CLOSED and WITHDRAWN and names no auction step. The ladder states LED_AUCTION, PROCEEDS_MATCHED and NO_BID_AT_70 are therefore read as stages of the LITIGATION machine on LitigationWorkflow, and the six auction facts are carried as elements of the two operations and as facts of the decision record. Three further values have no single source: the trigger of the step (the legacy AC1 says only that its trigger arrives, the FSD A2.19.2 names a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer and A2.19.4.4 declares no background event, and TSD S4 T5.3 declares no event), the operations of the three consumed owner contracts (the rwb-case case read, the rwb-case case-move answer with the enforcement task request and the rwb-decision rule package, named by no read source), and the requirement id (the legacy master carries none and the plan's reqs list for this slice is empty). The proceeds matching of R-LIT-65 is a second boundary of the same kind: the legacy story records the result, and the match, the application to the balance and the posting are P8's and the proceeds story's, so no proceeds row, ledger entry or balance change is written here.
evidence: TSD S4 T3.1 lists legal_action with id, case_id, law_firm_id, action_type, lawsuit_no, black_case_no, red_case_no, court_name, claim_amount, filed_date, judgment_date, judgment_amount, lit_status and status, and hearing with id, legal_action_id, hearing_date, hearing_type, outcome and next_date, with no auction field; T3.2 gives LOV-LEGAL-STATUS six values and LOV-LEGAL-TYPE incl. LED_AUCTION; T4 lists R-LIT-01 to R-LIT-25 and 54 more with LED_AUCTION, PROCEEDS_MATCHED and NO_BID_AT_70 only in the ladder rules; FSD S4 A2.19.2 gives Integration points LED portal and LIT and A2.19.4.4 gives None for a background event; TSD S4 T5.3 gives None for events and T5.2 sends the case to P3; the legacy story metadata table carries Epic, Module, Feature, Process, Priority, Depends on and Decision only; the plan row of RWB-S4-E5019-APP carries an empty reqs list; the context pack gives S4 two tables, zero events and zero jobs.
area: Data, workflow and traceability, S4 rwb-litigation
owner_role: S4 rwb-litigation service owner with the business analyst and the data steward
proposed: Keep legal_action and hearing unchanged, carry the six auction facts as elements of the two operations and facts of the decision record, hold the ladder states as stages of LitigationWorkflow, read the trigger as an auction signal of the workflow, build the three consumed reads against their owners' documents and fakes on Day 1 and trace the slice to REQ-S4-007.

title: The contract slice of RWB-E5-019 fixes an auction element, a timer element, three consumed owner operations and a baseline status that no source gives in full
source: Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 (T3.1, T3.2, T4, T5.1, T5.2, T5.3, appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2, appendix T-B); Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (A2.19.2, A2.19.3.1, A2.19.4); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-LIT-63 to R-LIT-67); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (feature row FEAT-LIT-19); _work/msr/context/S4.md (ownership rows of S4, naming and shared platform rules); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 and R7.2; AGENTS.md rules 9 and 10
section: CON s2, s3, s5 X4 and X5, s7 AC1, AC3, AC4 and AC5, s11 Data, s12.2, s12.5, s12.6, s12.8, s13, s19; the placeholders of both slices
description: The contract baseline has to name elements that no source read gives: the auction element of LegalActionRequest and LegalActionUpdate, the next-auction-date element of LitigationWorkflow, the operations of the three consumed owner contracts and the day counts behind the enforcement task due date. TSD S4 T-A.2 names LegalActionRequest, LegalActionUpdate and LegalAction but describes no auction field, the workflow catalogue gives LitigationWorkflow and no ladder activity, and no source names the rwb-case case read, the rwb-case case-move answer or the rwb-decision rule package operation. The four price bases and the 2 and 5 working days of R-LIT-65 and R-LIT-67 are values of the rule package and of reference data, so they are declared as values in force and never as schema defaults or code constants. The baseline status is a second gap: the FSD S4 v3 and the TSD S4 v2 are In review with empty sign-off tables and this run has no approval step, so the baseline is tagged at status Draft when its own contract tests pass and the sign-off is collected in the verification loop.
evidence: TSD S4 appendix T-A.2 describes API-S4-002, API-S4-003 and API-S4-004 with LegalActionRequest, LegalActionUpdate and LegalAction and no field list beyond the response name; T3.1 gives no auction field on either table; T5.3 gives None for events; appendix T-B leaves DL06 and DL11 open; the ownership rows of S4 list zero events and one workflow; the context pack gives two tables and five REST operations and no view; FSD S4 document control gives In review with an empty sign-off table and TSD S4 document control gives In review with an empty sign-off table; AGENTS.md rule 9 says a missing approval is recorded as an assumption and the work continues in Draft.
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-litigation with the solution architect and the owners of rwb-case and rwb-decision
proposed: Publish the auction element, the timer element and the three consumed rows with the placeholder until their owners confirm them, keep the four price bases and the day counts as package and reference values, and tag the baseline at status Draft on its passing contract tests.
